planningIntent.title: Planning intent
planningIntent.summary: Describes the general training direction, independently of races.
planningIntent.development: Development: progressively improve the group's capabilities.
planningIntent.base: Aerobic base: build or rebuild general capacity with conservative progression.
planningIntent.maintenance: Maintenance: preserve current capacity without significant progression.

planningAudience.sportingGroupHelp: The athlete's stable sporting classification within the team.
planningAudience.planningSubgroupHelp: A temporary planning audience made up of athletes from the same sporting group who share an objective.

Z1.name: Recovery / Regenerative
Z1.description: Active recovery and low-impact muscular adaptation.
Z1.effortAndPerception: Very easy. Comfortable jogging pace with virtually no effort.
Z1.biomechanicalFocus: Maximize diaphragmatic expansion. Relax shoulders and trapezius. Ideal for reinforcing clean, tension-free running mechanics.

Z2.name: Aerobic Endurance
Z2.description: Build the aerobic engine and improve efficient fat utilization.
Z2.breathingPathway: Nasal or mixed (inhale through the nose, relaxed exhale through the mouth).
Z2.biomechanicalFocus: Keep the rib cage stable. The core engages gently to absorb low impact. This is foundational work for the aerobic engine.

Z3.name: Tempo / Marathon Pace
Z3.effortAndPerception: Moderate. Conversation becomes broken into short phrases.
Z3.biomechanicalFocus: Coordinate foot strike and breathing rhythm to distribute impact load evenly and reduce postural changes caused by fatigue.

Z4.name: Threshold / Long Intervals
Z4.description: Lactate clearance and tolerance to high-intensity fatigue.
Z4.effortAndPerception: Hard. Only one or two words at a time.
Z4.biomechanicalFocus: An asymmetric pattern such as 2:1 alternates the side receiving impact during exhalation, when core stability is lower, helping distribute stress across knees and hips.

Z5.name: VO₂ Max / Sprints
Z5.description: Maximal oxygen uptake and terminal speed.
Z5.effortAndPerception: Maximal. Talking is impossible; breathing feels severely strained.
Z5.rhythmicPattern: 1:1 or free breathing with emphasis on exhalation.
Z5.biomechanicalFocus: At this intensity mechanics are constrained by respiratory demand. The mechanical goal is forceful carbon-dioxide clearance through strong exhalations; inhalation follows reflexively.
